top_choice_rationale: P003 (Helpman and Melitz, B014) credits one bounded discovery: productivity-sorted firms select into exporting and foreign investment, and trade reallocates resources across firms. The framework is over twenty years old, produced testable predictions that firm- and transaction-level data have largely confirmed, and spread across trade, macro and IO. The remaining weaknesses are the uncredited priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn, and the contested size of the welfare gains. The citation can narrow both by claiming only selection and reallocation, but I cannot fully resolve either from the supplied evidence. The B009 variants (P002, then P001) are very close on merit and I would support either. I place Autor-Hanson-Katz above Autor-Dorn-Hanson because the broader wage-structure evidence is the better-confirmed strand, and I treat the Dorn-or-Katz choice as unsettled. The B045 BLP method (P004) is a credible, mature, cleanly originated contribution, but it is narrower in reach and has an open Bresnahan attribution question. I still rank it above no award because it clears the bar of achievement and maturity.
